structure: Part 16 read the set's three spec ledgers under src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/spec/: decisions.json (schema of 97 rulings d-001 to d-097, each with subject conflict or behaviour, ruling resolve 44 / adopt 30 / park 23, resolution, rationale, decidedBy panel 75 / sam 22, decidedAt over four sittings, dissent on 43, escalate false on all, and supersedes / supersededBy on seven pairs), conflicts.json (40 conflicts c-001 to c-040, each with fields, sources, detail, resolution, resolvedBy panel 33 / sam 7 and the deciding ruling; none open) and backlog-extras.json (46 increments: 17 chore, 14 fix, 5 restore, 10 e2e; 32 in this repo, 10 in the tests repo, 3 in the plants backend, 1 in both). Since the earlier extract the only change to these ledgers is a rewording in five rulings (d-007, d-062, d-066, d-078, d-082) from records.finalise to records.submit, which changes no outcome, so all 187 earlier claims were kept with their ids. The claims run: ledger shape and counts (001-011), one claim per ruling (012-109), one per conflict (110-149), the backlog-extras increments that record a decision, departure or constraint (150-173), where the code matches or no longer matches a ruling (174-182), gaps in the ledgers (183-187), and new claims (188-200) for the records.submit wording and for recorded increments the code has since done (entry guard, Lighthouse scripts and workflow, end-to-end workflows, arm64 publish, concurrency group, security audit, weekly cron, SonarCloud, FIT job, Dependabot) or done differently (Dependabot's ESLint group). Panel rulings are part 17's.

claims.statement: Every notifier-facing string in the plants journey says Great Britain, not England, and the service applies no nation or territory check to the destination address, so a Scottish or Welsh destination is notified through this service; the draft SI's England-only drafting is recorded as a legal note and never rendered.
claims.quote: 'Great Britain' wins in every notifier-facing string (arrival-status heading and legend, arrivalDate labels by state, proposedPlaceOfLanding hint, confirmation body; the dashboard intro names no territory today — guidance-before-you-start) and the service applies no nation or territory check to the placeOfDestination address, so a Scottish or Welsh destination is notified through this service.

claims.statement: The journey collects exactly the statutory arrival matters: one arrival date for every commodity type, an arrival time only for potatoes, and an arrival status only for plants for planting and wood and cut trees; a potato notification is always framed as pre-arrival, a past date is accepted and flagged late rather than refused, and no actual-arrival date or time is added for potatoes.
claims.quote: Collect exactly the statutory matters: one arrivalDate for every commodity type; arrivalTime only when commodityType = potatoes; arrivalStatus only for plants-for-planting and wood-and-cut-trees.

claims.statement: The trader states whether the consignment has arrived on its own single-question page with Yes first, shown for plants and wood only and placed before the arrival details and destination pages; the service never derives the status from the date, and the destination page's already-arrived copy covers a consignment that has landed but not reached its destination.
claims.quote: The importer selects arrivalStatus on its own single-question page (plants and wood only, radios Yes first) before arrival-details and place-of-destination; the service never derives it from the date.

claims.statement: The arrival date is validated only as a real calendar date, with no sanity window and no animals-style bounds; the one bound is that an already-arrived date may not be after today in Europe/London, the date picker carries a maximum only in that state and never a minimum, expected dates accept any past or future day, and lateness is computed rather than validated.
claims.quote: arrivalDate validates as a real calendar date (dateText) with no sanity window and no animals-style bounds; the single bound is sourced — when arrivalStatus = already-arrived the date may not be after today in Europe/London (dateTextInRange, max only) because it is 'the date on which it first arrived'
claims.note: The GDS judge's one-year-each-way typo window and the policy judge's no-bound-at-all both lost; the typo window is parked, not rejected.

claims.statement: The timing windows are the draft SI's: plants and wood may be notified before arrival or no later than four days after the date of arrival, potatoes only before and at least two days before the expected date; lateness is calendar-day arithmetic in Europe/London that ignores the arrival time, notifying on the boundary day is on time, and the windows are shown up front as option hints on the commodity-type page and per state on arrival-status.
claims.quote: Lateness is calendar-day arithmetic in Europe/London and ignores arrivalTime — potatoes are late when the notification day is after arrivalDate minus 2 days, plants and wood when it is after arrivalDate plus 4 days (notifying on arrivalDate minus 2, or on arrivalDate plus 4, is on time)

claims.statement: A late notification is highlighted in four places and never blocked: a notification banner naming the rule breached on the confirmation page and on the read-only submitted check-your-answers view, a Late tag beside the status on the dashboard card, and warning text on the draft check-your-answers page when the entered date would make the notification late if submitted today, which says it can still be submitted; there is no separate late page.
claims.quote: before submission the DRAFT check-your-answers page shows govukWarningText when the entered date would make the notification late if submitted today, computed by the same helper with the request clock, and says it can still be submitted. It never blocks and there is no separate late page.
claims.note: The policy judge wanted the pre-submission warning parked and lost 2-1.

claims.statement: The late flag is a stored system value, not a read-time derivation: one pure helper computes on-time or late from the clock, the commodity type and the arrival date, the declaration POST commits its result immediately before submitting when the notification is a draft, and the confirmation page, the submitted check-your-answers view and the dashboard Late tag read the stored value and never recompute from the submission timestamp.
claims.quote: the declaration POST calls it with the finalise clock and commits the result as the lateNotificationIndicator system value (manifest obligation, system: true, in SYSTEM_POPULATED) immediately before submitJourney when the journey is DRAFT, leaving it untouched on a re-submit from AMEND
claims.note: The reason the flag is stored rather than derived is that the backend and the stub re-stamp submittedAt on every submission and keep no first-submission timestamp.

claims.statement: The ledger's first ruling on the arrival-status page (build the user-selected radios with Yes first for plants and wood, skipped for potatoes by a derived gate, never derived from the date) has been superseded by the owner's later ruling d-090, which keeps the same outcome in Save-and-continue terms.

claims.quote: Build the user-selected arrivalStatus radios page (Yes first) for plants and wood, placed before arrival-details and place-of-destination; potatoes have no status and skip the page by the derived gate. The service never derives the status from the date, in this run or later.

claims.statement: The England-versus-Great-Britain behaviour is adopted with Great Britain in every notifier-facing string and no nation check on the destination; the residual legal question (whether the draft SI is widened to Great Britain or Scottish and Welsh instruments mirror it) is recorded as parked inside the adopted behaviour and changes no page.
claims.quote: Build with 'Great Britain' in every notifier-facing string and no nation check on the destination address. claims.note: The GDS judge wanted the whole behaviour parked and lost 2-1 on labelling only; a behaviour carries one status, so the residual is recorded in the detail.

claims.quote: Seed potatoes are potatoes: commodityType = potatoes, the per-line category offers seed-potatoes and ware-potatoes, and a seed-potato line takes the reg 24A matters (variety, quantity, intended use, producer and crop ids, time of arrival, place of landing) and the two-day pre-arrival window.

claims.quote: The SI wording wins: the category value is conifer-wood-with-bark, labelled 'Conifer wood with bark, or isolated bark of conifer'. The mural table's 'with mark' is a transcription typo and carries no meaning.

claims.statement: The four wood caveats are scope conditions, not questions: they become the five wood category values with the bark, origin, height and form conditions in the value labels, the only extra wood data collected is size of tree and phytosanitary treatments, and nothing is asked about preservative treatment, bark condition or the three-metre threshold; the preservative exclusion moves from the treatments hint to a hint on the category question, worded with its cut-coniferous-trees exception.

claims.quote: The hardwood genus constraint is Castanea, Fraxinus and Platanus only. Juglans and Pterocarya are not offered anywhere in the service; the mural and Confluence lists that still carry them (and the mural spelling 'Juglens') are superseded by the SI footnotes.

claims.quote: All lines share the one commodityType chosen first; a consignment mixing potatoes with plants or wood is two notifications.

claims.quote: The list is set-owned reference data, not a hard-coded enum, and the details page offers only the entries allowed for the line's category — never fifteen with twelve rejected.

claims.quote: commodityType has three values (potatoes / plants-for-planting / wood-and-cut-trees) and the per-line category has nine (seed-potatoes, ware-potatoes, plants-for-planting, trees-for-planting, conifer-wood-with-bark, conifer-wood-without-bark, cut-coniferous-trees, hardwood-round-surface, hardwood-chips)

claims.quote: Both options get a neutral hint that lets the trader self-classify without policy knowledge; the genus list is not narrowed for trees for planting. Which plants-for-planting lines legally count as trees is a parked policy question, and the genus-derived alternative is not built.

claims.quote: Genus is a controlled list from the set-owned commodities service; species is required free text (requiredMaxText 58, no format check) on plants-for-planting and trees-for-planting lines until a species catalogue exists

claims.quote: with the four-country origin constraint on the second value alone. The Confluence and mural rephrasing is not modelled as a third value.

claims.ref: src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/spec/decisions.json d-029 (subject behaviour commodity-type-change-reconciles-lines, ruling adopt, status superseded, supersededBy d-092)
claims.quote: The on-load reconcile, three typed collections and retain-and-flag alternatives are not built; a model-owned projection helper is recorded as a candidate extension.

claims.quote: no pre-scope question and no 'you do not need to notify' page. Fuller scope text belongs with guidance-before-you-start, outside the journey pages. Explicit scope questions that end the journey are parked pending a policy answer, not built.

claims.quote: If ruled in later it is an onboarding step or a registration check before the dashboard, outside the notification journey and outside the obligations engine.

claims.statement: There is no regulator screen, filter or report in the plants frontend: what the journey owes the regulator is already collected as coded category, genus and ISO country of origin, a structured destination address, the arrival date and status, the late flag and a stable reference number, and the ledger corrects itself that no region is captured because the address block has no region member.
claims.quote: One correction: the detail must not claim a region is captured — the address block carries no region member and region derivation from the address is an open backend question under competent-authority-routing.

claims.statement: There is no inspector-side capture in this frontend: no outcome recording, no record of a non-notified consignment and no risk level; the notifier journey already gives inspectors the arrival status, the destination or current location, the coded commodity lines and the contact details, and nothing else is owed by the notifier.
claims.quote: No inspector-side capture in this frontend: no outcome recording, no non-notified-consignment record, no risk level.

claims.statement: There is no export or download feature in this frontend: the duty to analysts is discharged by storing structured coded values (ISO country, coded commodity type, category and genus, dates, arrival status, notification status), and extraction is backend and datalake work.
claims.quote: No export or download feature in this frontend. The journey's duty to analysts is discharged by storing structured, coded values (ISO country, coded commodityType, category and genus, dates, arrivalStatus, notificationStatus); extraction is backend and datalake work.

claims.statement: There is no admin or list-maintenance surface in this frontend and spot-check percentages and risk classifications are not represented in the notifier journey; what the run owes is that the commodity type, category, genus and origin allow-lists live in the set-owned commodities service behind a configuration seam, pinned by a whitelists test and never hard-coded in obligations or copy, so a policy list change is a data change.
claims.quote: the commodityType, category, genus and origin allow-lists live in the set-owned commodities service behind a configure* seam in routes.js, pinned by obligations/whitelists.test.js, never hard-coded in obligations or copy — so a policy list change is a data change.

claims.statement: There is no scheduling, appointment, check-booked step or notice to the trader: the only trace of checks in the journey is copy, namely the confirmation page's sentence that a spot check may be carried out at the place of destination without prior notice and the destination page's hint, which keeps a spot-check sentence in every state.
claims.quote: No scheduling, appointment, 'check booked' step or notice to the trader in this frontend; the hand-off to scheduling systems is backend work.
claims.note: The destination hint reads 'This is where a plant health inspector may carry out a spot check.' for potatoes and not-yet-arrived, and 'A plant health inspector may carry out a spot check here.' for already-arrived.

claims.statement: There is no documents collection, upload page, uploader route, virus-scan polling or document reference in this run; the ledger records that if a plants source ever names a document, the animals documents collection (up to ten uploads with the uploader and virus-scan polling) is the shape to copy.
claims.quote: No documents collection, upload page, cdp-uploader route, virus-scan polling or document reference in this run.

claims.statement: There is no outbox, no event publishing and no downstream routing in this run: the journey's only submission obligation is a synchronous submit that persists the whole answer snapshot, the confirmation page makes no promise about where the notification has gone, and when the hand-off lands the mapper must carry every statutory matter so the regulator receives the record intact.
claims.quote: the confirmation page makes no promise about where the notification has gone.

claims.statement: The plants dashboard lists plants notifications only, with no cross-journey By type filter, no Plants card label and no combined list; the Import Notification Service front door owns any cross-journey list later, and the ledger records that a trader importing both animals and plants uses two dashboards in this phase rather than papering the cost over.
claims.quote: A trader who imports both animals and plants uses two dashboards in this phase, and that cost is recorded rather than papered over.

claims.statement: Every element no source gives a format, unit or list for is a free-text input, required or optional as the statute says, with the animals maximum lengths (58 characters, 400 for the treatments textarea) and no format check; the only two rules beyond that are a 24-hour HH:MM rule for the arrival time, which is the one new validation factory, and a whole number of one or more for quantity with its hint corrected so it stops promising weight or volume.
claims.quote: arrivalTime gets a HH:MM 24-hour rule (the one new factory), and quantity stays a whole number of 1 or more with its hint corrected so it stops promising weight or volume.
claims.note: The ledger also corrects the spec's claim that EPPO codes are five or six uppercase letters: genus-level EPPO codes carry a leading digit, such as 1QUEG, so no pattern may be derived from that claim.

claims.statement: The intended use of potatoes stays a required per-line free-text element for potato lines, and the optional Use for plants and wood lines is not collected: the use obligation is deleted from the spec and from the commodity line item list, and reinstated as an optional per-line text input only if policy adds it to the statute.
claims.quote: delete the use obligation from the spec and from the commodityLines item list, and record it on the conflict as parked, to be reinstated as an optional per-line text input only if policy adds it to reg 26(2).

claims.statement: One obligation per concept: quantity per line, and country of origin, place of destination and arrival date per notification, with the label, hint and check-your-answers row label chosen from the feature's copy keyed on the commodity type and the arrival status; the potato-only extras (arrival time, proposed place of landing, producer and crop identification numbers) stay separate gated obligations, and check your answers, the overview and the dashboard must render the state label rather than the generic one.
claims.quote: Check your answers, the hub and the dashboard must render the state label, never the generic one.

claims.statement: The Confluence page's identification number of the potato produced is read as a typo for producer: the field is the producer identification number, labelled Identification number of the producer of the potatoes, with no model change.
claims.quote: 'Identification number of the potato produced' on the Confluence page is a typo for 'producer': the obligation is producerIdentificationNumber, labelled 'Identification number of the producer of the potatoes', exactly as the spec already has it. No model change.

claims.statement: The proposed place of landing is asked only for potatoes, with plants and wood notifications collecting no landing place, and it uses the animals port-of-entry autocomplete over the ports service backed by the reference-data ports-of-entry endpoint, which is built; the capture script's marker calling that endpoint unbuilt is recorded as stale and dropped.
claims.quote: The capture script's 'expected — endpoint not built' marker is stale and is dropped in the arrival-details increment; the value source is no longer a gate question.

claims.statement: The ware-potato origin list is Poland, Portugal, Romania and Spain, with Spain stored as the plain country code and the Balearic Islands exclusion carried by the origin page's inset for ware potatoes, so the country-of-origin hint stays verbatim animals; no region option is built and a region-level value is parked.
claims.quote: The SI wins: the ware-potato origin list is Poland, Portugal, Romania and Spain (ISO PL, PT, RO, ES); the mural's 'Spain & Poland' loses.
claims.note: The ledger records two corrections: the constraint entry naming Spain excluding the Balearic Islands is not a code the service can store, and the origin page cited a behaviour id that does not exist.

claims.statement: The first pass builds the origin question on the existing shared country block, whose captured membership covers every country the statute constrains to, and applies the per-category narrowing as validation inside the origin POST over the intersection of the allow-lists for the categories present on the notification: ware potatoes four countries, conifer wood without bark four countries, plants and other wood the member-State list, and seed potatoes any country in the block, with an out-of-scope origin refused by an error naming the allowed countries and check your answers re-running the same check.
claims.quote: with an out-of-scope origin rejected by an error naming the allowed countries, and Check your answers re-runs the same check. Naming a plants-specific reference-data block is parked in the end-anchored extra country-block-decision and blocks nothing.
claims.note: The hole the re-check closes: a ware-potato line added after origin was saved as France leaves a stored out-of-list origin, because wiping cannot purge a value on a list mismatch.

claims.statement: The origin value list by commodity is built as page-side validation: one country autocomplete on the animals widget and service, the origin POST refusing a country outside the allowed set with a narrowing error naming the allowed countries, the Balearic inset shown when a ware-potato line exists, and check your answers re-checking the same rule and refusing to submit with a Change link to origin; warn-or-accept, a Spanish region option, a plants-specific block and the grown-in versus originate-from wording are parked.
claims.quote: Check your answers re-checks the same rule and refuses POST with a Change link to origin. The warn-or-accept alternative, a Spanish region option, a plants-specific block and the grown-in versus originate-from wording are parked.
claims.note: Two policy silences are recorded rather than guessed: the statute scopes ware potatoes by where they were grown or suspected of having been grown while the collected matter is the country they originate from, and whether Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland count as the Common SPS Area for seed potatoes is an inference from the block name.

claims.statement: Nothing blocks the origin or arrival-details pages: countries stay on the shared block and the place of landing uses the built ports-of-entry endpoint, the only code change being to un-flag the ports target in the capture script; the proposed gated fix before the origin page is not created and the country-block question sits at the end of the backlog as an owner confirmation that gates no page.
claims.quote: The behaviour's proposed gated fix extra before the origin page is not created; the country-block-decision extra stays at the end of the backlog as a confirmation with Sam (type chore, gate sam), gating no page.

claims.statement: Standardising information is adopted only as far as a source allows: every element a source gives a list for is a coded value stored as a code and served from a set-owned or platform service (commodity type, category, genus, country of origin as an ISO two-letter code, place of landing as a port code, arrival status, notification status), and every other element is free text with a maximum length; controlled lists for intended use, treatment codes, a variety register, an EPPO lookup, a species catalogue and the commodity-code scheme are parked until policy names them.
claims.quote: Controlled lists for intended use, treatment codes, a variety register, an EPPO lookup, a species catalogue and the commodity-code scheme are parked until policy names them; the optional 'use' is removed (c-014).

claims.statement: The validation the service does is the kind that can only refuse a value that is not the thing the statute asks for: required-ness per the statutory mandate, membership for every coded value including the per-category origin narrowing and its check-your-answers re-check, a real calendar date, a 24-hour time, a whole number of one or more for quantity, the animals pattern for the consignment number, the animals maximum lengths for other text, and an HTTP 400 with an error summary on every failure; formats for the commodity code, the EPPO code and the three identification numbers are parked until a source names the scheme.
claims.quote: Formats for commodity code, EPPO code and the three identification numbers are parked until a source names the scheme; each becomes one lib/validate factory with default messages in both copy files when ruled.

claims.statement: The reference number keeps the animals shape, minting point and display places (the journey strip, the dashboard card title, the confirmation panel and the read-only check-your-answers view) and the frontend prints exactly what the backend or stub mints, today a two-digit year and six characters with no prefix, inventing, parsing and validating nothing; the type-code prefix is a parked backend-and-stub decision whose owner-gated increment moved to the end of the backlog so the review section can ship.
claims.quote: the frontend prints exactly what the backend or stub mints — today {YY}-{XXXXXX} with no prefix — inventing, parsing and validating nothing.
claims.note: The anchor moved because the build loop stops on an owner-gated increment, and the anchor protected nothing: the reference is minted at record creation on the dashboard Start POST, so the unique-index migration applies from the first draft wherever the increment sits.

claims.statement: The notification status the trader sees is the engine lifecycle of draft, submitted, amending and deleted shown as the animals tags with the same colours on the journey strip, the dashboard card and the confirmation page, and nothing richer; lateness is the separate late flag and is never folded into the status, all four values are reachable because amending after submission is in scope, and where the confirmation prints the status it prints the tag label rather than the raw constant.
claims.quote: Where the confirmation prints the status it prints the tag label, never the raw constant. Any richer importer-facing vocabulary (late, selected for check, checked, non-compliant) is parked pending a policy vocabulary; check outcomes are inspector-side data outside the notifier journey.

claims.statement: The animals post-submission action set is in scope minus Copy as new: a submitted notification offers View, Amend and Delete on the dashboard, a draft offers Resume and Delete, an amendment offers Resume, Cancel amendment and Delete, the read-only check-your-answers view offers Delete when submitted and the Cancel amendment link when amending, and the confirmation page restores the animals block on how to view or amend the notification.
claims.quote: dashboard SUBMITTED shows View | Amend | Delete; DRAFT shows Resume | Delete; AMEND shows Resume | Cancel amendment | Delete; the CYA read-only view offers Delete when SUBMITTED and the Cancel amendment link when AMEND
claims.note: The late flag is computed once at the first submission from draft and left untouched on a re-submit from an amendment; the date of notification stays the record's latest submission timestamp. Two policy questions are recorded as parked, not blockers: whether an amended arrival date should re-run the timing test, and whether the backend should keep a first-submission timestamp.

claims.statement: The plants reference-number type-code prefix is parked as a policy answer nobody has: the first pass builds on the unprefixed format the backend and stub mint, shown verbatim in every display place, and the cross-repo owner-gated increment stays on the backlog anchored at the end so its gate does not halt the review section.
claims.quote: Parked: the plants type-code prefix is a policy answer nobody has (still an open question on epic EUDPA-407 as of this ruling).

claims.statement: The notification status vocabulary adopted is the four engine lifecycle values shown as the animals tags Draft blue, Submitted green, Amending yellow and Deleted grey on the journey strip, the dashboard card and the confirmation page, with lateness carried by the separate Late tag and banner; a richer importer-facing vocabulary is parked, and check outcomes never change the importer-facing status in this run.
claims.quote: the animals tags Draft / Submitted / Amending / Deleted (blue / green / yellow / grey) on the journey strip, dashboard card and confirmation page as the notification status the importer sees

claims.statement: The post-submission actions are adopted with the delete-notification and cancel-amend confirmation pages copied from animals as their own increments; Copy as new stays parked, and the policy questions (whether a submitted notification the regulator has acted on may still be amended or withdrawn, and whether an amended arrival date re-runs the timing test) are recorded as parked rather than blockers while the late flag freezes at the first submission.
claims.quote: The policy questions — may a submitted plants notification the regulator has acted on still be amended or withdrawn, and does an amended arrival date re-run the timing test — are recorded as parked, not blockers; meanwhile the late flag freezes at the first submission.

claims.statement: Submission is synchronous and must stay so: the confirmation page renders only once the record is submitted with its date stamped server-side at that moment, a failed submit re-renders the declaration with the recoverable-error message and never an optimistic confirmation, a not-ready submit returns to check your answers, and no queue, batch or optimistic confirmation may be introduced between the trader's submit and the persisted record.
claims.quote: No queue, batch or optimistic confirmation may be introduced between the notifier's submit and the persisted record.
claims.note: The ledger corrects a judge's wording: a thrown submit re-renders the declaration with the recoverable error, and only a not-ready submit redirects to check your answers.

claims.statement: The shared page chrome ships verbatim in the first pass: the service name Import notification service in the service navigation, page-title suffix and dashboard heading, the Alpha phase banner with the existing service-desk feedback address, and the Address book and Manage account links pointing nowhere; the confirmation help block says only to contact the relevant plant health authority, naming APHA, the Forestry Commission and Scottish Government, with no email, telephone or opening hours, and the page is flagged provisional copy.
claims.quote: The confirmation help block says only 'contact the relevant plant health authority — APHA, the Forestry Commission or Scottish Government' with no email, telephone or opening-hours lines, and the page is flagged provisionalCopy.
claims.note: The owner-gated chrome increment is narrowed to six decisions nobody can make today: the service name, the feedback address, the helpdesk contact lines, the homes of the two links, and the footer accessibility-statement and privacy-notice URLs. Three items come off that gate and build now: the unauthorised-view copy move, the compose file and the stack-check wiring.

claims.statement: The plants dashboard is a set-owned page at the service root that lists only the plants notifications this session knows, scoped to the signed-in organisation and excluding deleted ones, with one summary card per notification carrying the status tag and the late tag, and no By type filter, no cross-journey rows and no journey-type label on the cards.
claims.quote: No 'By type' filter, no cross-journey rows and no journey-type label on the cards.
claims.note: The session-only listing means a trader returning in a new session sees an empty list; the empty-state copy is honest about it and the fix is sub-parked as a user-model matter with decidedBy sam.

claims.statement: The panel's first ruling on the journey shape (an opening run over the section order landing on the overview, a four-group task-list hub with five statuses, section captions from a map, and a flow-only declaration page as the submit gate) has been superseded by the owner's ruling d-087, which replaces the run with one Save-and-continue rule ending at check your answers.
claims.ref: src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/spec/decisions.json d-069 (subject conflict c-034, ruling resolve, status superseded, supersededBy d-087)
claims.quote: Plants has all four, mirroring animals: an opening run over the spec's section order landing on the hub, a four-group govukTaskList hub with the five animals statuses, section captions from a captionSections map, and a flow-only declaration page as the submit gate.
claims.note: The superseded wording carries two corrections that survive: the commodity-details entry sub-page is never a step of the journey order, and the overview lands with no task rows, each section's first page adding its own row.

claims.statement: The plants service name, the feedback address, the helpdesk contact lines and the homes of the Address book and Manage account links are parked: the first pass keeps the inherited chrome verbatim and the plain competent-authority help sentence, and to close the question the service owner must name the service and supply the feedback and helpdesk route the Mural board leaves to be confirmed, with the front door owning the two links.
claims.quote: To close it the service owner must name the service and supply the feedback and helpdesk route the mural leaves TBC, and the INS front door must own the two links

claims.statement: There is no eligibility checker and no before-you-start page: the need to understand whether goods are in scope is met inside the journey by a dashboard introduction that names the scheme and the three commodity groups and links to GOV.UK guidance only when a real URL exists rather than a dead link, by commodity-type option hints quoting the statutory timing windows in the statute's own words, and by per-field hints; an in-service is-my-consignment-high-risk checker is recorded as a later start-section page, not rejected.
claims.quote: links to GOV.UK guidance only when a real URL exists (a copy leaf, never a '#' link)
claims.note: One correction the ledger forces on the hints: the policy section's shortened four-days wording drops the statute's 'before or', so the commodity-type option hints quote the regulations rather than the policy section.

claims.statement: The previous national notification scheme and the Northern Ireland and Republic of Ireland services are parked as a copy and value-list input only, with no first-pass change: the statutory data list fixes what is collected, so a precedent can only refine page copy, the potato intended-use options and the identification-number and commodity-code formats, and a precedent-driven change lands later as a copy or validation edit, never a model change.
claims.quote: A precedent-driven change lands later as a copy-pair or lib/validate edit, never a model change.

claims.statement: Three standing build constraints apply to every increment because the commodity list and the statute will change: every commodity-type, category, genus and origin list is data behind the set-owned commodities service rather than an obligation or a copy literal; the two statutory timing windows are single named constants exported from one module beside the arrival-details feature and read by the lateness rule and by any hint naming a window, so no other copy of the number exists; and the territory wording and the authority names are copy leaves. A reissued policy paper is then a data or copy change, never a model change.
claims.quote: A reissued policy paper is then a data or copy change, never a model change. The go-live date and who re-runs the digest are delivery notes outside the spec.

claims.statement: Accessibility is adopted at page level: every plants page ships an automated accessibility check on its initial and validation-error states plus a Lighthouse accessibility floor, and the check's tag list is widened from the two WCAG 2.0 tags to five covering WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 AA so the machine-checkable 2.1 and 2.2 rules actually run; the manual WCAG 2.2 audit and this service's own accessibility statement are parked, and the footer accessibility link is routed through the owner-gated chrome increment.
claims.quote: the axe tag list is widened from the two WCAG 2.0 tags to ['wcag2a','wcag2aa','wcag21a','wcag21aa','wcag22aa'] so the machine-checkable 2.1 and 2.2 rules actually run.
claims.note: This knowingly diverges from the animals two-tag list on the strength of the policy paper's WCAG 2.2 AA requirement; a violation the wider list surfaces is a finding to fix, never a reason to narrow the list.

claims.statement: Meeting GDS standards is adopted as already delivered by the engine conventions (GOV.UK Frontend components only, one thing per page, error summary, task-list overview, check your answers, confirmation panel and the Alpha phase banner), with the Service Standard assessment recorded as a programme event outside the spec; a plain-English sweep of every copied animals string for animal nouns is added as a rider.
claims.quote: A plain-English sweep of every same-as-animals string for animal nouns is added as a rider; the one known instance (countryOfOrigin error copy) is already conflict c-027 and is ruled there, not here.

claims.statement: The data-protection governance items are parked because the policy paper supplies none of them and the panel must not invent them: the lawful basis, the privacy notice content and URL, and the retention of drafts and submitted notifications. What the first pass owes it already does: it collects only the statutory matters plus the paper's Common Data, scopes every record to the signed-in organisation, takes no document upload, and keeps the footer Privacy link whose destination resolves under the owner-gated chrome increment.
claims.quote: Park the governance items — lawful basis, privacy notice content and URL, retention of drafts and submitted notifications — because the policy paper supplies none of them and the panel must not invent them.
claims.note: A judge's guess that the lawful basis is a legal obligation under the draft statute was dropped as exactly the invention the standing ruling forbids. Production retention is undefined because the backend stamps an expiry only outside production.

claims.statement: Secure internal login is parked: the policy paper's security requirement speaks only of internal users, who this frontend does not serve, so the notifier keeps Defra ID sign-in, the stub session with authentication still enforced, and organisation-scoped records, and nothing more is built; whether policy accepts Defra ID as the external identity, and the Mural board's registration stage, are out of this phase.
claims.ref: src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/spec/decisions.json d-077 (subject behaviour nfr-secure-internal-login, ruling park, decidedBy sam)
claims.quote: Annex 6 item 4 speaks only of internal users, who this frontend does not serve; the notifier keeps the Defra ID OIDC sign-in, stub session with auth enforced, and organisation-scoped records exactly as already adopted, and nothing more is built.

claims.statement: The journey's share of round-the-clock availability is adopted as already delivered: save and return, recoverable save and stale-action banners that keep the trader's answers, a synchronous submit with no long work, and a lateness rule computed in Europe/London so a submission at any hour is judged on the right calendar day. Nothing in the journey may gate submission by time of day; peak-load targets and a plants performance suite are parked as infrastructure follow-ons.
claims.quote: Nothing in the journey may gate submission by time of day. Peak-load targets and a plants k6 suite are parked as infrastructure follow-ons; platform availability is the CDP SLA.

claims.statement: A live Welsh service is parked: the first release ships English only with the page language set to English, the copy seam stays exactly as adopted so every plants string lands in both locale files at once, no Welsh is invented, and the runtime locale switch is not built because it is new engine capability and no translation has been commissioned; shipping half-Welsh machine drafts behind a toggle is recorded as serving Welsh speakers worse than a clean English-only release.
claims.quote: the first release ships English-only with html lang en, the copy seam stays exactly as adopted so every plants string lands in both locale files at once, no Welsh is invented, and the runtime locale switch is not built
claims.note: The bilingual requirement is the policy paper's own, so it cannot be rejected; whether English-only is acceptable for a first release is recorded against the release rather than resolved. The follow-on plan is written into the behaviour in full so it can be cut as one increment the day a translation exists.

claims.statement: Minimising trader effort is both a goal and a ceiling: every question must trace to the statutory matters or the policy paper's Common Data list and no increment may add one that does not, any future optional question carries the word optional and never gates readiness, and the three effort-savers stay parked under their own behaviours.
claims.quote: every question must trace to the SI or the Common Data list and no increment may add one that does not; any future optional question carries '(optional)' and never gates readiness.
claims.note: A judge's phrasing that nothing outside the statutory data list may be mandatory was corrected, because the Common Data contact obligations come from the policy paper's annex 6 and are required.

claims.statement: The policy paper's single word Sustainable is parked with no reading adopted: nothing in the journey depends on it, the behaviour stays so the non-functional list is complete, and policy is asked what was meant before anything hangs on it; a judge's maintainability reading was refused as an invented meaning, though the record notes the existing dependency and documentation hygiene increments would already serve it.
claims.quote: 'Sustainable' is a single unqualified word in the only source that uses it, nothing in the journey depends on it, and the panel adopts no reading

claims.statement: The journey's share of the eight management-information metrics is adopted as already carried: coded commodity type, category and genus and an ISO country of origin for the first three metrics, and the record's created and submitted timestamps for the sixth; the journey measures nothing and adds no question for reporting, and the definition of time taken per notification stays a parked policy question with created-to-submitted as the interim reading.
claims.quote: the journey measures nothing and adds no question for MI. The definition of 'time taken per notification' stays a parked policy question with created-to-submitted as the interim reading.
claims.note: One verified gap is recorded: the plants backend list projection carries no submitted timestamp, so the dashboard's Date submitted row is empty in real mode and the sixth metric cannot be read from the list. The animals frontend has the identical hole.

claims.statement: Equal access for Defra Policy, Scottish Government and the Forestry Commission is parked as a multi-organisation user model for the regulator product, wholly outside the notifier frontend; the journey owes it only the full submitted record with no organisation-based withholding, and its one touchpoint is the confirmation naming all three competent authorities without preferring one.

claims.quote: the journey owes it only the full submitted record with no organisation-based withholding, which it already persists, and its one touchpoint — the confirmation naming all three competent authorities without preferring one — is already in the spec.

claims.statement: The two copy tripwire tests (the copy-convention test and the English-Welsh copy-parity test) are rewritten in the same commit as the first feature folder rather than as later increments, because an increment is its own pull request whose checks run the test suite, so a pull request leaving both tripwires red can never merge; the two restore increments are withdrawn into the dashboard increment's plan.

claims.note: The ledger records that the orchestrator applied this on 2026-09-06 and the owner had not yet confirmed, with the instruction to supersede the decision to reverse it.

claims.statement: The owner's October ruling that the journey ends on check your answers rather than the overview, that check your answers shows an unfinished notification and names every outstanding task, and that its Continue re-shows the page with those errors, has been superseded by the November ruling d-086; only the declaration and confirmation wait for a complete notification.

claims.statement: Save and continue goes to the next page in the journey's one page order that applies, from every start; when that page needs a required earlier answer that is missing, such as the commodity type or the country of origin, it goes to the page that asks for it, and the page it opens is always one the overview offers; from the last page that applies it goes to check your answers even when the notification is incomplete.

claims.quote: Save and continue goes to the next page in the journey's one page order that applies, from every start.

claims.statement: Back goes to where the trader came from, and the trail keeps the newest 40 places, past which the oldest drop and Back ends at the overview; on check your answers reached with nothing saying where the trader came from, Back goes to the overview on a draft or an amendment and to the dashboard once the notification is submitted and after a cancelled amendment.
claims.ref: src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/spec/decisions.json d-086 (subject behaviour opening-run, ruling adopt, decidedBy sam)
claims.quote: Back goes to where the trader came from; the trail keeps the newest 40 places, past which the oldest drop and Back ends at the Overview.

claims.statement: The plants journey has all four shape features mirroring animals: Save and continue over one page order ending at check your answers, a grouped task-list overview with the five animals statuses whose groups come from the flow sections, section captions from a map, and a flow-only declaration page as the submit gate; the commodity-details entry sub-page is no step of the page order, because its Continue returns to the commodities list whose Continue advances.
claims.ref: src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/spec/decisions.json d-087 (subject conflict c-034, ruling resolve, decidedBy sam, supersedes d-069)

claims.statement: The register records that territorial scope was stated three ways across the sources (the draft statute says into England and landing in England, one of its own clauses says intended destination in Great Britain, the policy section says arrival in GB, and the user needs and the Mural board say EU to GB), with Scottish Government a competent authority yet the statute England-only; it is settled by ruling d-001 on the Great Britain wording.

Provisional pick: 'Great Britain' in all notifier-facing copy (closest to the Policy section and to reg 26(2)(b)); the arrival and destination labels carry it. Gate question: does a Scottish or Welsh destination notify through this service?

claims.statement: The register records that potatoes want an expected time and date of arrival with no post-arrival wording while plants and wood want an expected date of landing or the date first arrived with no time, and that no source says whether a late potato notification asks for the actual arrival time and date; it is settled by ruling d-002.

claims.quote: no source says whether a late potato notification asks for the actual arrival time and date. NNS-UN-035 wants one date field whose label switches.

claims.quote: 'Consignment Number' is undefined: no issuer, no format, and reg 24A never uses the word consignment.

claims.statement: The register records that seed potatoes sit under Plants for planting on one Mural image but under Potatoes on the Mural data-fields board, in the draft statute and on the Confluence requirements page; it is settled by ruling d-017, which makes them potatoes.

claims.quote: which a service could derive from the arrival date being past or future — but not reliably on the day of arrival.

claims.statement: The register records that the Confluence page's four additional caveats for wood products could not be read as scope, as extra data, or as both, and that the Mural author offered them in case that level of detail was needed; it is settled by ruling d-019, which makes them scope conditions in the category labels.

claims.quote: the extractor could not tell whether they define which wood is in scope, which wood needs extra data, or both.

claims.quote: the extractors read '(for plants for planting)' as qualifying species only, but it may qualify genus and species together.

claims.quote: Every Confluence-derived fact in this spec is therefore a snapshot (requirements v5 2026-07-02, user needs v11 2026-06-30) that may lag the workbook.

claims.quote: No source gives a format, unit, value list or validation rule for any free-text element

claims.quote: A single mixed consignment (several genera, or several potato varieties) cannot be described by one line.

claims.quote: but the draft SI reg 26(2) lists only matters (a)-(i) and Annex 2 / Annex 6 list nine plants/wood items — no 'use'.

claims.quote: Read as a typo for 'producer'. Provisional pick: producerIdentificationNumber, label 'Identification number of the producer of the potatoes'.

claims.quote: four entries (Olea europaea, Nerium oleander, Polygala myrtifolia, Salvia rosmarinus) are species not genera.

claims.quote: Same practical scope, different wording.
